source_title: How to Unlock & Use JOONAS in Moon Sweepers - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Cleaning the moon manually definitely takes a lot of time in Moon Sweepers , especially when your base is already busy processing dust and expanding its production lines. That is where J.O.O.N.A.S. comes in. This autonomous cleaning robot travels across the Moon, collects dust, and sends it back to your base without you having to drive a vehicle .
However, getting it to work takes more than just spending money on the robot and turning it on. You need a Capsule Catcher and a suitable production setup. This guide explains how to use J.O.O.N.A.S. in Moon Sweepers and what problems you might run into.
How to Get J.O.O.N.A.S. in Moon Sweepers
J.O.O.N.A.S. becomes useful once you have progressed far enough to afford late-game automation . You can buy it through the Services menu for $20,000 .
After purchasing the robot, open the Build menu and select J.O.O.N.A.S. to place it on the lunar surface. You can position it near an area that needs cleaning or send it to an area that’s inconvenient for you to reach.
Getting the robot is only the first part of the setup. J.O.O.N.A.S. collects lunar dust and stores it in capsules , which it launches when they are full. Those capsules need somewhere to land before you can send their contents into your production system.
As such, you’ll need a Capsule Catcher , which costs $1,500. This brings the minimum investment for one working setup to $21,500, excluding conveyor belts and any extra equipment required to process the collected material.
How J.O.O.N.A.S. Works in Moon Sweepers
J.O.O.N.A.S. is designed to take over lunar cleaning while you concentrate on other activities . Unlike equipment that works within a fixed area, this robot can travel across the surface to find more areas that need to be cleaned.
Once deployed, it moves around the Moon and clears dirty areas in sections. Its movement might look a little unpredictable, especially if you expect it to walk in a straight line. Don’t worry, though, as the robot is intended to operate autonomously rather than requiring you to guide every movement.
As it collects lunar dust, the robot fills its internal capsule. When the capsule reaches capacity, J.O.O.N.A.S. shoots it to the nearest Capsule Catcher. The receiver collects the capsule and lets the material enter your production system if all connections are in place.
After launching a capsule, the robot can continue its cleaning cycle and gather more dust. This creates a repeating process that requires much less direct involvement than manually sweeping the lunar surface.
The Capsule Catcher is a must-have if you want to turn J.O.O.N.A.S. into a useful part of your production network. J.O.O.N.A.S. sends its capsules toward the nearest available catcher. Without it, the robot has no designated receiver for the capsules it ejects.
Once you’ve bought a Capsule Catcher, place it near the area where your robot will be working . Then, connect its output to a conveyor belt leading toward your Depot.
If your production line already processes lunar dust through equipment such as a Pressure Chamber, you can connect the catcher to that system instead. Avoid building an unnecessarily complicated system before testing the basics.
Just remember that a J.O.O.N.A.S robot can clean the Moon and launch capsules successfully, but the collected material will not reach its intended destination if the conveyor connection is incomplete.
Is J.O.O.N.A.S. Worth Buying in Moon Sweepers?
J.O.O.N.A.S. can be a valuable addition to a late-game base in Moon Sweepers . They come in handy if you have already automated most of your existing production and want to reduce the amount of manual cleaning required .
Start with one J.O.O.N.A.S. and check that it works reliably in your current setup. Once it has completed many cleaning cycles and delivered its capsules successfully, you can decide whether another unit would improve your production.
It can make resource collection more convenient, but its value depends on how reliably it operates in your set up.
Can multiple J.O.O.N.A.S. robots use one Capsule Catcher?
Yes, multiple robots can use the same Capsule Catcher when they are within range. However, each robot sends its capsules toward the nearest catcher, so many units might send their output to the same receiver. Make sure your conveyor network can handle the additional material.
Why does J.O.O.N.A.S. stop working when I move away?
Some players have reported a bug that causes J.O.O.N.A.S. to stop cleaning whenever they travel too far away from it. If you run into this issue, the first thing you should try is returning to the robot and checking whether it resumes working once you're back in range. That said, there is currently no confirmed workaround that guarantees continuous operation at a distance, so you may need to stay relatively close for reliable results. As a precaution, make sure your game is updated to the latest version, since patches can sometimes resolve these kinds of issues.
